title: Sriwijaya Air 182

location.name: Java Sea, approximately 11 nm NW of Jakarta

summary: Boeing 737-500 crashed into Java Sea four minutes after takeoff from Jakarta during a climb to 11,000 feet. The aircraft experienced thrust asymmetry when the autopilot commanded reduced power: the left engine thrust decreased as directed, but the right engine thrust lever remained stuck at climb power due to excessive mechanical friction in the throttle cable. The resulting yaw and roll to the left caused the autopilot to reach maximum deflection. When the autopilot disengaged following the pilot's activation of the stabilizer trim switch, the aircraft entered an upset and descended rapidly into the sea. The pilots were unable to recognize the asymmetric thrust condition or recover from the upset.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by a faulty autothrottle system that was unable to move the right thrust lever due to friction or binding within the mechanical control cable system. The thrust asymmetry resulting from this mechanical failure, combined with pilot error in failing to recognize and correct the aircraft's developing roll and yaw, and inadequate upset prevention and recovery training, led to loss of control and impact with the Java Sea.

factors.evidence: The autothrottle attempted to move the throttle levers back when the aircraft reached 11,000 feet on ATC instruction, but the right lever remained stuck at climb power due to excessive friction in the throttle control cable (p. 1-2)
The right engine thrust lever remained stuck at climb power due to excessive friction, while the left lever moved backward as commanded, creating an asymmetric thrust condition (p. 1-2)
The autothrottle problem had been reported 65 times since 2013 and was never resolved; maintenance troubleshooting did not identify the mechanical friction in the throttle cable (p. 131)
The pilots did not recognize the thrust lever asymmetry or the aircraft's deviation from the intended flight path before it developed into an upset condition (p. 135)
When the bank angle reached 37 degrees, the Enhanced GPWS Bank Angle warning activated, startling the pilots (p. 1-2)
Automation complacency and confirmation bias led to reduced active monitoring of the thrust levers and flight path (p. 135)
Sriwijaya Air's upset recovery training program lacked detail and guidelines to ensure pilots had adequate knowledge to prevent and recover from upset conditions effectively (p. 135)
The aircraft entered an upset condition and descended rapidly into the Java Sea approximately 4 minutes after takeoff (p. 1)

events.text: Flight SJ182 departed from Runway 25R, Jakarta in daylight conditions with 62 occupants (2 pilots, 4 flight attendants, 56 passengers) aboard
Autopilot engaged at approximately 1,800 feet in LNAV mode and MCP SPD mode
At altitude 5,400 feet and 220 knots, pilot changed autopilot directional control from LNAV to HDG SEL mode
Autopilot vertical control changed to V/S mode and autothrottle changed from N1 mode to MCP SPD mode, requiring less engine thrust
At altitude 7,950 feet, left thrust lever began decreasing while right thrust lever remained at 46 degrees due to mechanical friction
ATC instructed aircraft to stop climbing at 11,000 feet
At altitude approximately 10,250 feet, aircraft turned left instead of right as intended due to thrust asymmetry, with calculated spoiler deflection of 3.7 degrees
Enhanced GPWS Bank Angle warning activated when bank angle reached 37 degrees to the left
Pilot called out 'ONE THREE ZERO' in response to new climb clearance to 13,000 feet
Aircraft entered upset condition with excessive bank angle; overspeed warning sounded; CVR recording ended as aircraft descended into Java Sea

recommendations.text: Include a requirement of UPRT (Upset Prevention and Recovery Training) in the CASR Part 121 and develop detailed guidance to increase the effectiveness of upset prevention and recovery training implementation

Review the requirements of notification of rescue coordination center in the CASR Part 170 to ensure compliance with ICAO Annex 11 standards, specifically including the alternative conjunction (or) in the determination of emergency states
recommendations.outcome: DGCA reviewed and amended CASR Part 170 to align with ICAO Annex 11

recommendations.text: Consult the DGCA prior to modifying any flight operation procedure and obtain No Technical Objection (NTO) from Boeing prior to modifying any existing aircraft manufacturer flight operation procedures
Increase the number of data retrieval in the Flight Data Analysis Program (FDAP) to improve the ability of monitoring flight operation safety performance (target above 28.1% average)
Emphasize the hazard reporting program to all employees (pilots, maintenance, dispatchers, and ground personnel) to encourage hazard reporting and identification

safety_changes: Sriwijaya Air implemented Upset Prevention and Recovery Training (UPRT) program starting November 2021
DGCA conducted special inspection of all Boeing 737-300/400/500 aircraft in Indonesia regarding AD compliance and pilot training
Sriwijaya Air revised Flight Data Analysis Program event definitions to include thrust asymmetry and loss of control events
Sriwijaya Air amended maintenance procedures for handling repetitive defects and autothrottle troubleshooting
DGCA amended CASR Part 170 to align with ICAO Annex 11 for emergency state determination
